title: Dublin crèche software provider Little Vista reports security incident exposing children's and parents' data
date_note: RTÉ's page of 24 November gives no earlier day for Little Vista's email to providers; it says an external party contacted the company the previous Thursday.
geo_basis: RTÉ describes Little Vista as a Dublin-based childcare management software operator
summary: RTÉ reports that Little Vista, a Dublin-based childcare management software operator, told affected organisations of a security incident giving unauthorised access to data. An external party who contacted the company showed that children's names, dates of birth, profile photos, and parents' and staff contact details could be accessed. Little Vista says it found no evidence its core database was accessed and has secured the affected system.
plain: A Dublin company that makes software for childcare centres says someone outside the company could reach children's and parents' details. It says it has secured the affected system.
exec: Childcare providers using outsourced software may hold children's data exposed through a supplier; RTÉ quotes Brian Honan saying responsibility stays with the crèche.
action: As cybersecurity specialist Brian Honan advises in RTÉ, crèches should get assurances from Little Vista and other outsourced providers that adequate security is in place; staff and parents should be alert to unexpected contact.

validation.note: Only RTÉ was read; it quotes Little Vista's email to providers. The company's own notice was not read. RTÉ gives no count of crèches or children.

review.note: Compared data types, core database statement, Honan advice, date against RTE page
